reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports the first four premises for a specific HEA (CoCrFeMnNi) under specific conditions, but it provides no evidence for the fifth premise—that the same mechanism and a pre-treatment to induce it will work for a different alloy (FeNiCrCoCu). The hypothesis overextends the evidence by assuming transferability without support.
premises: Dynamic amorphization can produce an ultra-nanocrystalline surface layer during sliding in a single-phase HEA (CoCrFeMnNi) in inert conditions.
This ultra-nanocrystalline layer is associated with low friction (~0.3) and remarkably low wear rates (~10^-6 mm^3/N-m).
The dynamic amorphization model accurately predicts grain size-dependent shear strength in the inverse Hall-Petch regime for that HEA.
The beneficial wear and friction behavior is linked to the formation of the ultra-nanocrystalline layer, not to oxidation or mixed oxide films.
These findings can be directly extended to a different HEA (FeNiCrCoCu) and to a pre-treatment that induces dynamic amorphization during sliding.
